id_and_class.summary: Peirce treats phenomenal consciousness as Firstness, the simple, unanalyzable quality of feeling, which he finds by inventorying whatever appears to mind (phaneroscopy). Every experience also contains Secondness (brute reaction) and Thirdness (habit, law, meaning), so experience is continuous with sign-use and inquiry. In his metaphysics feeling comes first in the cosmos and matter is ‘effete mind’ hardened into habit.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Firstness, the Pure Quality of Feeling

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is Firstness: a quality of feeling (redness, pain, cheerfulness) that is simple, partless, and what it is regardless of anything else. Peirce adds that a quality in itself is a mere possibility, and becomes conscious only in degrees.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Synechism, Peirce's doctrine of continuity, denies any break between mind and matter. Matter is mind whose habits have hardened into physical laws, so body is a settled form of mind.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable at the cosmic level, since the universe begins as ‘a chaos of unpersonalized feeling’. Within an organism, conscious states rise by degrees out of unconscious qualia and sink back into unconscious habit.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Peirce starts from appearances without first assigning them to an inner subject or an outer world. A person is a kind of general idea, a coordination of ideas, and all thought works through signs, so directedness is a matter of semiosis (Thirdness).
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are Firstness: monadic, positive qualities known in immediate feeling. Because feeling is immediate, it is ‘veiled from introspection’; by the time one asks what the present instant contains, the question comes too late.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Three irreducible categories (quality, reaction, mediation); signs and their interpretation; habits that become laws; a continuous, feeling-suffused universe in which even protoplasm feels.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through phaneroscopy, a disciplined observation of appearances that sets aside questions of truth and physiology and trains the artist's eye (seeing the blue shadows on snow). Peirce denies any power of introspection or intuition: we know our inner life only by inference from external facts.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Every phaneron shows Firstness, Secondness, and Thirdness. Psychologically these map onto three graded modes: primisense (feeling), altersense (awareness of otherness and reaction), and medisense (synthesis, thought, learning). The living present spans the percept, a fresh memory (ponecept), and an immediate anticipation (antecept).

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (Firstness); reactive awareness; thought and learning; time-consciousness; cosmic mind.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The three categories, applied to all experience: quality, brute reaction, and mediation by signs and habit.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness is continuous and graded. It emerges from unconscious qualia, organizes itself through sign-processes, and fades into unconscious habit as actions become routine.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Pervasive and graded across a continuous cosmos, extending well beyond human subjects; Peirce holds that protoplasm genuinely feels.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Thirdness gives consciousness its work: interpreting signs, forming and revising habits, and driving inquiry. Habits make action efficient but also make us see what we expect instead of what is given.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Thirdness mediates and synthesizes qualities and reactions into meanings, and synechism treats the stream of experience as continuous.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: All thought is in signs. Experience is a structured field where qualities, shocks, and meanings operate together, and knowledge of the inner world is inferred from outer signs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Cosmic rather than biological: the universe evolves from undifferentiated feeling toward habit and law, and physical regularities are mind grown inveterate.
core_claims_and_evidence: Phaneroscopy shows three irreducible categories, Firstness, Secondness, and Thirdness, present in every appearance.
Phenomenal consciousness is Firstness, a simple quality of feeling that is immediate yet hidden from introspection.
We have no faculty of introspection or intuition; all self-knowledge is inference and all thought is in signs.
Matter is ‘effete mind’, with inveterate habits becoming physical laws, and synechism denies any gap between mind and matter.
Peirce fixed his categories in 1867, more than three decades before Husserl's Logical Investigations, which supports reading him as an independent founder of phenomenology.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological description (phaneroscopy) combined with logical analysis and speculative metaphysics.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: None directly. Champagne links Peirce's critique of habit to inattentional blindness and smartphone distraction, and Nöth reads his graded consciousness as anticipating current debates on the conscious/unconscious boundary.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Peirce set his categories in 1867 from Kant's table before adopting phenomenological language, so critics such as Sonesson and Champagne say his phenomenology presupposes its results. Husserlians object that fusing quale with possibility confuses the mental act with its object. Short questions the coherence of his objective idealism, and Hookway confines his phenomenology to deriving the categories.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether Firstness-as-possibility explains phenomenality or only relocates the problem remains open. Peirce left his phenomenological method largely undeveloped, and most of his system sits in unpublished manuscripts.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Descriptive phaneroscopy stands apart from the speculative cosmology, so a reader can accept one without the other. The idealism links him to panpsychist and process views, though his stress on habit and law separates him from constitutive panpsychism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since feeling pervades a continuous cosmos and mind shows up wherever signs are interpreted, Peirce's view does not confine consciousness to humans or brains. He did not address machines.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: A person is a general idea and consciousnesses are continuous with one another, which leaves room for some form of persistence, but Peirce's account settles nothing about individual survival.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: It follows from his objective idealism that the universe itself grows from feeling toward habit, law, and meaning, so mind is part of the cosmos's own development.
